name: WebGL/WebGPU Browser Implementations
text:
# WebGL/WebGPU Browser Implementations

Also called: Browser-based GPU Volume Rendering

## Overview
This family implements [direct volume ray casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) within web browsers using WebGL or WebGPU APIs, solving the problem of rendering volumetric data without plugins by adapting GPU-accelerated [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) to browser-specific constraints like the lack of 3D texture support in WebGL 1.0 or WebGPU's memory alignment rules [G]. It differs from desktop GPU implementations by prioritizing web standard compatibility and handling browser-specific data encoding workarounds, such as packing depth into [RGBA](#5142-color-packing-rgba.md) channels or using 2D texture atlases [G].

## Subtopics

### [WebGL Multi-pass Ray-casting with 3D Geometry Intersection](6575-webgl-multi-pass-ray-casting-with-3d-geometry-intersection.md)
Enables interactive coexistence of volumetric datasets and 3D triangular meshes in WebGL by using a [multi-pass rendering](#6224-two-pass-and-multi-pass-techniques.md) pipeline to handle occlusion, blending, and [ray intersection](#7624-ray-ray-intersection.md). It sets itself apart from single-pass approaches by explicitly separating depth, surface color, and volume traversal into distinct passes to correctly manage back-to-front blending and geometry intersections. Choose this method when rendering opaque and transparent 3D geometry within or alongside volume data in WebGL environments.

### [WebGL Path Tracing Volume Rendering](8592-webgl-path-tracing-volume-rendering.md)
An interactive voxel volume renderer using path tracing that runs in modern browsers via WebGL 2.0. It sets itself apart from [standard ray casting](#12643-standard-ray-casting.md) by computing normals via central differences of opacity and applying Phong-like lighting with soft shadows, rather than relying solely on direct illumination. Choose this method when lighting and shadowing effects are required for volumetric data in WebGL 2.0.

### [StructuredVolumeRenderer](17796-structuredvolumerenderer.md)
[StructuredVolumeRenderer](#17796-structuredvolumerenderer.md) is a reusable, graph-native GPU renderer for scalar, vector, and hybrid volume data in WebGPU environments. It sets itself apart from sibling WebGL implementations by leveraging WebGPU's storage [buffer and texture](#15685-texture-buffer-object-for-block-types.md) binding models, manual trilinear interpolation, and fixed-step jittered ray marching with early [opacity termination](#1019-early-ray-termination.md). Choose this method when rendering structured grid data (buffers or 3D textures) in WebGPU with explicit memory control.
